title: Rabbi Reuven ben Itztrobli
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: The leading sage of the generation in the time of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, as in Me’ilah 17a: once the government decreed that they should not keep Shabbat and should not circumcise their sons, etc. Rabbi Reuven ben Itztrobli went and cut his hair in the komi style, went and sat with them, and through his wisdom the decree was annulled. Afterward they recognized that he was a Jew and decreed again, and they sent Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yose to Rome to annul the decrees.

Two precious sayings of his remain to us: in Moed Katan 18b Rav said in his name, “From the Torah, from the Prophets and from the Writings [we learn] that a woman is [destined] for a man from the Lord”; and he further said there in his name: “A person is not suspected of something unless he did it,” etc.

In Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim, chapter 9, end of halakhah 4, it is related that two sons of Rabbi Reuven Istrobilos were students of Rabbi. Rabbi saw that the Angel of Death was looking at them and gnashing his teeth. (Rabbi) said: “Let them be exiled to the South; perhaps exile atones.” When they came there, they died (for “a person’s feet…,” etc.).

notes.text: וסיפר קומי is haircutting in the komi style, and מ״המ is the Angel of Death. The truncated feet saying is left abbreviated. The two sons’ episode is not converted into an additional contemporary identity claim.

The consulted sons-and-Angel-of-Death episode is in Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3, while Hyman supplies the end of 9:4. The full Hebrew and Guggenheimer’s English actor-control passage were read: Rabbi sees the angel looking at the sons and grinding his teeth, orders exile, and the angel takes them there. Hyman’s abridgment remains distinct from the preceding Solomon story.
